1. This is a reference petition u/s 18 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act"), filed by the petitioners mentioned aforesaid for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Land Acquisition Collector (NorthWest) (hereinafter called 'the LAC') for acquisition of their land for public purpose.
The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the LAC no. 410 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Jai Bhagwan & Ors. v.
Union of India Page no. 3 of 14 Act, Government intended to acquire about 907 Bigha 09 biswas of land with its specification mentioned in the notification for public purpose namely 'Rohini Residential Scheme' under the "Planned Development of Delhi".
3. The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (21)/2004/L&B/LA/28049 dated 18.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 907 Bigha 9 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Rani Khera, Delhi.

The actual physical possession of the said land is with the petitioner as the physical possession of the land has not been taken and the respondents shall take possession thereof from the petitioner.

The LAC passed the award in a mechanical way without applying the mind and without going through the claim filed by the petitioner, as such the award is not acceptable to the petitioner, and she has received the awarded amount under protest and without prejudice to their rights.
The LAC failed to take note of the actual and practical market value of the said land and had adopted a narrow approach while observing that no proof of claim market value is attached.
The LAC has not assessed the actual market value of the said land in spite having knowledge of the fair market value adjudicated by the courts.
The LAC has failed to properly appreciate the quality, status, potentiality and development of the said land and its surroundings.

sentences.text: However, no specific separate additional evidence for enhancement of compensation has been led.
19. I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under :  WHETHER THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED FOR ENHANCEMENT IN COMPENSATION, IF YES, THEN TO WHAT EXTENT ?
OPP 20.
The onus of proving the aforesaid issue is on the petitioner.
It is settled proposition of law that the onus to prove the market value of the said land or inadequacy of compensation awarded by LAC is always upon the petitioner.

The aforesaid proposition of law has been authoritatively held by our Hon'ble Supreme Court in State of UP & Anr. v. Rajender Singh, AIR 1996 SC 1564 as under:
"The onus is on the petitioners to prove that their lands are capable of fetching higher compensation then what has been determined by the LAC and that he is entitled for enhanced compensation".
LAC no. 410 / 2016 (Award No. 08/200506/DC(NW)) Jai Bhagwan & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 11 of 14 21.

During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 06.01.2023 and Ld.

Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioner may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
22.
Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

23. Since the fair market value of the land situated in village Rani Khera are covered by the award in question has already been determined by this court, this court has no reason or evidence to deviate therefrom.
In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioner is concerned.

24. In the Mukhtyar Singh (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Rani Kera acquired through Award No.08 of 200506 dated 12.07.2005 as Rs. 19,73,583/ per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).

The petitioners are, accordingly LAC no. 410 / 2016 (Award No. 08/2005 06/DC(NW)) Jai Bhagwan & Ors. v. Union of India Page no. 12 of 14 entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Mukhtyar Singh (supra).

25. The petitioner has not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioner.
RELIEF 26.

In view of the findings on Issue No.1, the petitioner is granted the following reliefs:
(i) Fair Market value of land of petitioners as mentioned in the revised statement u/s 19 of the Act @
Rs.19,73,583/ per acre.
An enhancement of Rs.4,03,583/ per acre is accordingly accorded.

(ii) Additional amount @ 12% (in terms of Section 23(1A) of the Act).
(iii) Solatium @ 30% on the enhanced compensation ( in terms of S.23 (2) of the Act).
(iv) Interest @ 9% per annum for the first year and 15% per annum for the subsequent year till the payment of enhanced compensation by LAC is made (in terms of Section 28 of the Act).
